hints: Compare the current through the 10 Ω resistor and the 1 kΩ resistor. Is it the same?

Across a fixed 9 V, more resistance lets less current through. Power, the heat made each second, is P = V² ÷ R. So the lower-value resistor gets hotter. Think of two hoses on the same tap. The wide one lets far more water rush through.
Swap in the 1 kΩ resistor and check its power reading. Is it under the 0.25 W rating?
